reason: Chat stream follow fixes (UI-1, UI-2, UI-3, UI-7, UI-8). Backend: provider frames carry a runtime epoch and a finished runtime's frames stay readable for late viewers (follow_provider_turn, /chat/turns/{id}/events), callback_required names its wait kind, ChatTurnSummary reports wait_kind/wait_summary/subagent_ids/recoverable, /state and /session-activity treat an interrupted turn awaiting recovery as busy and stoppable, and restart recovery settles a goal turn its policy never resumes. Python selection: test_chat_stream_follow.py (new regression tests for each of those), test_chat_reconnection.py and test_session_state.py (follow cursor and snapshot contracts), test_chat_goals.py (goal resume/cancel with interrupted turns), test_restart_recovery_lifecycle.py and test_chat_subagent_lifecycle.py (the recovery pass and subagent stop this change settles through), test_playwright_impact.py (new areas), test_chat_api.py and test_chat_subagents.py in full (follow, stop, late followers, pending-turn summaries, subagent waits and resume), and the test_chat.py nodes that exercise stop, naming during a live turn, and restart recovery. Frontend: streamChat pause/epoch handling, the follow-authority decision, catch-up read cursor, callback status copy, plus the existing chat connection, client, stream lifecycle, message reconciliation and session-state tests. Playwright: SessionsPage changed, so entry:assistant/{desktop,mobile-chromium,mobile-webkit}; the new mocked journeys at 320/390/430 on Chromium and WebKit (area:chat-stream-follow) and real-Core LAN journeys (area:chat-stream-follow-core); callback, paused-supervisor, subagent, chat-reconnection and goal-lifecycle areas that share the changed follow paths.
